project.name: Receipt Studio

summary.description: Receipt Studio is a local-first Electron point-of-sale and structured thermal-receipt designer for Windows. It stores shops, products, customers, templates, printers, and sales locally without a database or cloud account.

features.feature: Multiple shops with locally stored logo assets
Products, customers, completed sales, and immutable sale snapshots
Clickable receipt sections with visible selection outlines
Configurable, scannable QR codes across preview, PDF, and ESC/POS
Installed Windows and USB printer discovery
ESC/POS encoding presets with real byte conversion
Fixed-canvas label designer with custom sheet dimensions
System, ZPL, and TSPL label printing
Product-bound price labels with name, price, SKU, stock, barcode, and QR fields
Strict separation between POS receipt printers and product label printers
Direct ESC/POS printing over TCP port 9100
Validated JSON backups and automatic rotating backups

fromRelease.step: Download the Setup executable from the GitHub Releases page.
Run the installer and launch Receipt Studio.
Create a shop during first-launch setup.
Configure and test the receipt printer before the first live sale.

procedure.step: Find the installer and portable executable in the release directory.
Create a GitHub Release and attach both executables.

release.signing: Release executables should be Authenticode-signed before public distribution to reduce Windows SmartScreen warnings.

storage.notes: Writes are validated with Zod and use temporary files followed by atomic rename. Logo files are copied into the application user-data directory.

network.applicationTest: Open Printers, select Print test, choose a saved receipt template, and print it with sample data through the same path used for real sales.
network.note: The computer and printer normally need to be on the same local network. A successful socket write does not prove that paper physically printed.

printer.usb: USB printing uses a printer installed through the Windows printing system and requires the appropriate Rongta Windows driver.

architecture.component: Electron lifecycle, IPC, storage, PDF, diagnostics, and printing

security.control: no generic renderer filesystem or socket access

contributing.step: Fork the repository and create a focused feature branch.
Add or update tests for behavioral changes.
Run every quality command before opening a pull request.
Describe user-visible changes and printer-specific considerations.
